issues.description: raise PerformanceWarning conflates a warning class with a hard exception
issues.detail: PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass but is raised as an exception, mixing notification with abort. Decide the policy: warn-and-proceed via warnings.warn, or refuse the write with a properly named exception (ValueError/ConfigError). The current shape leaves callers unable to reason about behavior and the docstring/PR description contradict the implementation.

issues.description: Unreachable break after raise inside the misalignment loop
issues.detail: The break statement immediately follows raise PerformanceWarning(msg) and can never execute. This dead code reveals the loop's postcondition was never stated: report-all, fail-fast, or warn-and-continue. Decide the intent and write it cleanly, removing the unreachable statement.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size computation is arithmetically suspect and uses meaningless max(1, itemsize) guard
issues.detail: np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize) papers over an invariant (itemsize is always >=1 for real dtypes) and presents a value to the user whose relationship to array.chunk-size config is not linear. Either assert the invariant and drop the guard, or state the precondition you are advising the user to satisfy rather than inventing a number.

issues.description: Divisibility check only inspects dw[0]; loop invariant about uniform chunks is unstated
issues.detail: The audit examines only the first chunk size per axis and renders a verdict for the whole axis. normalize_chunks can return ragged tails, and any non-uniform interior block would be silently missed. State the invariant explicitly (all interior chunks equal, tail is shape % dw[0]) or check every element.

Python parses this as not ((nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw) == 0), which is the intended meaning only by precedence accident. A reader should not need to consult an operator table to verify a correctness check. Rewrite as nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0.

issues.description: Test asserts pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning), locking in the wrong contract
issues.detail: The test pins the warn-as-exception confusion in place and will obstruct any correction toward warnings.warn. Once the warn-vs-raise policy is decided, switch to pytest.warns or pytest.raises(ValueError) and rename the test to match its actual assertion (currently named *_warns but asserts raises).

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously refuses this diff as under-reasoned. The core defect is conflating "warn" with "raise": PerformanceWarning (a Warning subclass) is used as a hard exception, followed by an unreachable break, and the test locks this confusion in as the contract. The safe_chunk_size formula is dimensionally suspect and uses a meaningless max(1, itemsize) guard rather than stating an invariant. The per-axis check only inspects dw[0] and relies on operator-precedence-dependent syntax. Decide the warn-vs-raise policy first, state the loop's invariant and postcondition, then rewrite the check and test against the stated contract.
